attacks.claim: Removing a single center (for example, at its request) leaves offline copies showing in color until their `valid_until`. The artifact states this openly and bounds it to the forecast validity window, but the plan has no faster purge for a licensing or legal withdrawal.
attacks.evidence: "its zones disappear within 10 min and any offline copies expire at their `valid_until`."

attacks.claim: Offline expiry relies on device time. The guard only catches a clock earlier than the download time. A clock set back to a point after download but before real expiry would still show an expired rating in color. This needs deliberate tampering or a large clock error, and it is a known limit of offline-first designs.
attacks.evidence: "if the device clock reads earlier than that, the stored forecast is treated as expired."

attacks.claim: The rollback text says the flag takes effect on next foreground, while QA verified the purge on next launch. Phones that stay offline and never open the app will also not receive the flag, so "no stale ratings remain on phones" is stronger than what was verified.
attacks.evidence: "takes effect on next app foreground" vs QA "offline forecast data purged on next launch"

attacks.claim: The `bbox` parameter has no stated bounds, cache-key normalization, or CDN TTL, and the 92% hit rate and $140/month origin cost are given without evidence. The per-IP limit may also throttle users behind shared IPs. The impact is limited because origin failure degrades to gray expired zones rather than wrong ratings.
attacks.evidence: "GET /avy/v1/zones?bbox=…" ... "rate limited at origin to 120 req/min per IP" ... "92% CDN hit rate"

attacks.claim: The claim that location is not sent sits beside a bbox-based endpoint. The viewport and IP can reveal approximate area of interest in server logs. Retention for logs and analytics is not stated.

Legal review (LGL-902) is stated for the card text and terms-of-use update only. The blog post naming all 19 centers is not shown as reviewed, and the agreement's attribution and marketing terms are not tied to the map layer and legend. The go/no-go check at 10:00 has no named owner.
attacks.evidence: "Card text and the terms-of-use update were reviewed by legal (LGL-902)."
